notes: Added: · The video editor now offers Metadata next to Export whenever a project has something to hand over, so a session you come back to after a restart — or after its video is already rendered — can go straight to the generator instead of being asked to export the same video again. It carries the beat, title and producer across, and points the YouTube Upload page at your last export. · The Metadata generator's Options panel has a Hashtags & tags section with "Repeat tags under the hashtags": the YouTube tag list then closes the description, one blank line below the hashtag block. Templates that already print a tag wall there are left as they are, and the block is dropped rather than push the description past YouTube's 5000-character cap. · The Beat platform tab follows the YouTube tab on its own. Whenever the title, style, mood, tag seeds or the generated title, description and tags change up there, the store listing's title, description, keywords, genres, moods and instruments are rewritten here — hashtag blocks, tag walls, keyword walls and the BPM/key lines (which the listing prints for itself) are removed, and genres, moods, tags and instruments are picked out of the style, mood and tag-seed fields, with the hand-typed keywords leading the three store tags. Typing into one of these fields — or Pause sync — stops the rewrite, so your own wording stands; Re-sync from YouTube hands the fields back to the YouTube tab. · The YouTube and Beat platform tabs carry a glyph each, so the publish target and the store read apart before their labels are. · The Template panel now carries a second family: the store listing's body is no longer stuck with one shape. Clean listing writes the support line, the specs, then the genre, mood, instrument and tag lines; Description only keeps the support line and specs and leaves those categories to the store's own fields; Storefront adds a 🛒 purchase line with your beat store link at the foot. A profile saves both choices — the YouTube template and the store-listing one — so applying it restores the shape of both listings, and the Beat platform tab names the chosen layout under its generated listing. · Fixed: · Dragging an image on the preview canvas moves that image again, instead of dragging the cover out from under it. The shapes layer and the images layer each span the whole frame, and the shapes layer sat above the images layer, so a press on an image was taken by the shapes layer's empty background and fell through to the cover's pan. Both layers now own only what they draw — shapes, images and their handles — while a press on genuinely empty space still pans the cover and clears the selection. · A selected image's whole outline is now part of its drag. The dashed border it draws sits just outside the image's own box, and a press on that border was taken by the cover behind it: the border — the natural place to grab — moved the background while the image sat still. The corner handles, the rotation dot and the image's own transparent pixels all behave the same way now, and the ring around an image no longer pans the cover. · An unfilled shape no longer takes a press in the empty middle of the rectangle it outlines. A shape claims only what it paints — its outline, or its fill where it has one — so an image sitting under an outline-only shape can be dragged straight through it. A selected shape still answers anywhere inside its box. · The canvas cannot move the cover out from under something you can see. A press that lands on a shape, an image, one of its handles or a text line belongs to that object; if it cannot be served, nothing moves — where before the background panned. The cover still pans from genuinely empty space, exactly as it did.
